feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 0 and the iteration 7 confirmation both gave 52.28 with five 12 mm sensors at y 0.05 m, mass 0.8, wheel_radius 0.03 and wheel_track 0.12, with progress 0.138 (oval) and 0.148 (s-bend) and about 1.0 line loss per run. Iterations 1 to 2 showed that 16 mm sensors at y 0.04 and 0.03 m lowered progress (oval about 0.11, s-bend about 0.13) without removing the single loss. Iteration 8 showed that 8 mm footprints lowered progress on every track and raised slalom loss to 2.0, so 12 mm is the footprint to keep. Iteration 6 raised oval progress to 0.1446 but lowered s-bend progress to 0.135 with the larger radius and track, so those dynamics stay at baseline. Steering oscillation has stayed between 0.07 and 0.14 throughout, so the loss is a dropout at a fixed point, not jitter. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If progress holds at or above 0.138 (oval) and 0.148 (s-bend) with line loss at or below 1.0 per run and slalom at or below 2.0, keep y 0.06 m and ask for per-track telemetry on where the single loss occurs before any further geometry change. (2) If progress falls below baseline on either track while line loss stays at 1.0, return to y 0.05 m, which is the best-measured offset, and treat the forward offset as tuned. (3) If line loss rises above 1.0 on oval or s-bend, or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.2, return to y 0.05 m and test controller changes on the Integrator side rather than further sensing changes.
requested_changes: Keep sensor_size 0.012 m on the five-sensor layout (x -0.02 to +0.02 m at 10 mm spacing), with wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg, and move sensor y from 0.05 to 0.06 m. Basis: iterations 0 and 7 at y 0.05 m gave the best progress (0.138 and 0.148), iterations 1 to 2 at 16 mm and y 0.04 to 0.03 m lowered progress, and y 0.06 m has not been tested.

If progress drops below baseline on the oval or s-bend, return sensor y to 0.05 m and do not move the offset further. Basis: iteration 0 (y 0.05) beat iteration 2 (y 0.03), and iteration 8 showed that changes to the 12 mm baseline have so far lowered progress.

If line loss stays at 1.0 per run with baseline progress, test wheel_radius 0.035 m with wheel_track 0.12 m, changing only the radius. Basis: iteration 6 changed radius and track together, raised oval progress to 0.1446, and lowered s-bend progress to 0.135, so the two effects have not been separated.
